seo.title: Mì Quảng in Da Nang: The Authentic Local Dish to Try First
seo.meta_description: Discover authentic local food in Da Nang, including mì Quảng with pork and egg, bún mắm, and grilled rice paper rolls.
seo.body_markdown:
## Mì Quảng: The Signature Dish of Da Nang

Mì Quảng is the defining dish of the Quảng Nam–Đà Nẵng region. It features rice noodles served with shrimp, pork, a hard-boiled egg, roasted peanuts, and fresh herbs. A small amount of rich, turmeric-spiced broth tops the bowl. This dish is widely recognized as a local staple and is deeply rooted in Central Vietnamese tradition.

The flavor profile is bold, spicy, and savory—characteristic of Central Vietnam. The chili peppers (ớt) used are strong even when small, so visitors should prepare for a fiery experience. Mì Quảng is best enjoyed in local eateries, especially those serving the traditional Quang Nam-style version with chicken, quail eggs, and snakehead fish.

## Bánh Tráng Cuốn Thị Heo – A Street Food Staple

Bánh tráng cuốn thịt heo (grilled rice paper with pork) is a staple of Da Nang’s street food culture. Thin, grilled rice paper rolls are filled with boiled pork, fresh vegetables, green mango, and a local dipping sauce. This dish is widely available and popular among locals and tourists alike.

It is often found in night markets and small roadside stalls.

## Bê Thui Cầu Mống – A Regional Delicacy

Bê thui Cầu Mống originates from Cầu Mống village in Điện Bàn district. This slow-roasted veal dish has golden skin and is typically served with fresh rice paper, herbs, and mắm nem (fermented anchovy sauce). It is a regional delicacy that reflects Da Nang’s rural culinary roots.

This dish is best experienced in local eateries that serve traditional Central Vietnamese fare. It pairs well with a side of rice and is ideal for those who enjoy rich, savory flavors with a strong umami depth.

## Bún Mắm – A Bold, Local Favorite

Bún mắm Bé Hà at 130 Bùi Hữu Nghĩa offers a strong fish sauce rice vermicelli dish. The aroma of fish sauce is noticeable from afar. The rice crackers are highly recommended. This dish is not for the weak of palate and is a great choice for foreign tourists seeking authentic local flavors.

It is served in a casual setting and is widely appreciated for its bold taste and traditional preparation.

[source:7a53903a-827d-4092-88d2-9653482d4a25](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Da_Nang)

seo.title: Authentic Pho at Thìa Gỗ Restaurant in Da Nang
seo.meta_description: Discover authentic pho at Thìa Gỗ Restaurant in Da Nang, a comfortable setting for traditional Vietnamese street food without relying on street vendors.
seo.body_markdown:
## Authentic Pho at Thìa Gỗ Restaurant

Thìa Gỗ Restaurant in Da Nang offers real Vietnamese cuisine with a focus on authentic pho. Located at 53 Phan Thúc Duyện, the restaurant serves many traditional street food dishes in a more comfortable, indoor setting. This makes it ideal for visitors seeking authentic Vietnamese food without the hassle of street vendors.

The staff are very friendly and the experience is welcoming. While the service may take a bit longer, the quality of the food remains true to homemade styles. It’s a reliable option for those who want to enjoy traditional Vietnamese dishes in a clean, accessible environment.

## Complete North Vietnamese Meal at Cơm Nhà Linh

Cơm Nhà Linh at 35 An Thượng 26 offers a full set menu with meat, fish, soup, vegetables, peanuts, and eggs. This North Vietnamese-style meal is perfect for those who want a complete, local experience. The option to grill meat at the table adds a hands-on touch, making it feel like a home-cooked meal.

While the service can be slow, the food quality and authenticity are unmatched. It’s a great choice for anyone seeking genuine Vietnamese flavors in a familiar, home-style setting.

## Traditional and Modern Desserts in Da Nang

Da Nang’s dessert culture blends Vietnamese tradition with French influence. Traditional chè (sweet soups and puddings) are still widely available, often sold at local markets. Modern options like Nutella-stuffed brioche reflect the city’s francophone roots.

These desserts are available at market stalls and roadside vendors, offering a taste of local culture. For those who enjoy sweet endings to meals, Da Nang provides a rich variety of traditional and modern treats.
